solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Hurry to serve up set point

indicators.note: to serve something up is to present it freshly arranged, so these letters are dished out in a new order

explanation.surface: A tennis player is urged to get on and serve when it is set point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'serve up' rearranges SETPOINT; 'to' is a link. The tennis surface hides the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom to step on it (the accelerator) means to go faster, so to hurry.

clue.text: Plan article on Circle Line

parts.note: the is the definite article
O is shaped like a circle
Ry is short for railway, a line

explanation.surface: A scheme for London Underground's Circle Line.
explanation.walkthrough: The Circle Line is a London Underground route; here each word works separately.
explanation.definitionFit: A theory is a proposed scheme or idea of how something works, loosely a plan.

clue.text: Help and agility needed to capture beast

indicators.note: the words capture, or hold, the answer within them

explanation.surface: A zoo team needs assistance and nimbleness to catch an animal.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'helP AND Agility'.
explanation.definitionFit: A panda is a black-and-white bear, an animal or beast.

clue.text: See blonde concealing nasal spray?

indicators.note: the letters are disguised, concealed in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A blonde seems to be hiding a decongestant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concealing' rearranges SEEBLONDE. The question mark flags that the spray is blood, not medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: Blood spurting from the nose is humorously described as a spray from the nose.

clue.text: Colossal loss in the main?

definitions.meaning: the main is the open sea; the famous liner sank there in 1912

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means gigantic, and the liner of that name was the most famous loss at sea.

clue.text: Equality is hard in church district

parts.note: par means equality, as in 'on a par'
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A claim that everyone in a church district is treated equally is a tough one.
explanation.definitionFit: A parish is the area served by one church and its priest, a church district.

clue.text: Gentleman getting up in the afternoon — the object's transparent!

indicators.note: one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: pm stands for post meridiem, the afternoon

indicators.note: in a down clue, getting up means reading the word from bottom to top

parts.note: sir is the address for a gentleman

explanation.surface: A man rising after noon claims his intentions are clear.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'getting up' reads the gentleman's title upwards as RIS. The definition is cheeky: the exclamation jokes that the late riser's purpose is see-through.
explanation.definitionFit: A prism is a block of glass or crystal, a see-through solid that splits light.

clue.text: Your label changed colour

indicators.note: the letters are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Somebody's label was given a new colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' rearranges YOURLABEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal blue is a deep, vivid shade of blue, a colour.

clue.text: Careless hit-and-run

parts.note: a slap is a hit
a dash is a short run

explanation.surface: A careless hit-and-run accident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is a link; 'hit-and-run' looks like one compound but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Slapdash work is done hastily and carelessly.

clue.text: Perfect score: one dividing bridge partners in game

parts.note: ten is the top mark in many judged sports

indicators.note: one piece splitting another means it sits inside it

parts.note: North and South are partners at the bridge table, N and S
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A game report: a perfect ten, with one player coming between the bridge partners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dividing' puts I between N and S, giving NIS after TEN. In bridge the four seats are North, South, East and West, with North-South one partnership.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennis is a racket sport, so it is an example of a game.

clue.text: Hysteria developing by December 31

indicators.note: something developing is changing its form, so the letters take a new shape

explanation.surface: Panic is mounting as the year-end deadline approaches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developing' rearranges HYSTERIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Something due before the end of the current calendar year is due within this year, by its last day.

clue.text: Money box that takes the biscuit?

parts.note: bread is slang for money
a bin is a box or container

explanation.surface: A cash box that wins the prize for outrageousness.
explanation.walkthrough: To take the biscuit means to be the most outrageous; here it is read literally, as a container a biscuit might be put in.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen container for loaves can literally hold, or take, a biscuit too: a playful reading of the idiom.

clue.text: Complaint made by youngster getting through month

indicators.note: a piece getting through another goes inside it, so it sits within

parts.note: May is a month of the year
a lad is a young boy

explanation.surface: An illness a child caught that lasted the month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made by' is only a link; 'getting through' is the container signal, picturing the boy passing through the month.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint in the medical sense is an illness or ailment, just like a malady.

clue.text: Varnish from two countries

parts.note: French is the adjective of France
Polish is the adjective of Poland

explanation.surface: A wood finish imported from a pair of nations.
explanation.walkthrough: The two pieces are the adjectives of two countries, France and Poland, read together as one phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: French polish is a shellac varnish rubbed on to give furniture a high gloss.

clue.text: Quickly getting beside river first

indicators.note: the river is placed first, ahead of the other piece

parts.note: the Forth is a Scottish river
with can mean alongside or beside

explanation.surface: Hurrying to the riverside before anyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' is a link. The Forth flows into the sea at Edinburgh.
explanation.definitionFit: Forthwith means immediately, without delay, so quickly.

clue.text: All raise a glass here (not you, Private!)

definitions.text: All raise a glass here (not you, Private!)

parts.words: All raise a glass here (not you, Private!)
parts.note: a drinking place open to all and sundry, the opposite of private, where everyone may raise a glass

explanation.surface: Everyone drinks a toast, but the lowly soldier is left out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Private' reads as a soldier, but it is the opposite of the first word of the answer. A British pub traditionally had a cheaper basic bar and a smarter lounge.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub's basic bar, open to all, is where everyone gathers to drink.

clue.text: Not working out

definitions.meaning: workers refusing to work in a dispute are not working
workers who are out have walked off the job

explanation.definitionFit: Workers who have downed tools in an industrial dispute are idle, or out.

clue.text: In time, Diana's message… it's impossible to destroy

parts.note: an era is a period of time
Di is the short form of the name Diana
a cable is a telegram, a message

explanation.surface: A message from Diana declaring something is indestructible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's' is a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ineradicable cannot be rooted out or wiped away, so it is indestructible.

clue.text: One responsible copper finding pair in bed in Calais

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: lit is the French word for bed

explanation.surface: A policeman finds a couple in bed in a French port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a policeman but gives the chemical symbol. Calais is a French port, so 'in Calais' asks for French.
explanation.definitionFit: A culprit is the person to blame for an offence, the one responsible.

clue.text: You've seen it before: Jade upset for all to see after five

indicators.note: the second piece comes after the other
upset means knocked over, so the letters are disturbed

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral five
U is the British film rating meaning universal, suitable for all

explanation.surface: Jade's distress is public, after a group of five.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' makes DEJA from JADE.
explanation.definitionFit: Déjà vu is the feeling of having already experienced something, as if seen before.

clue.text: And other things belonging to the lady engraver

parts.note: etc, short for et cetera, means and other things
her is the possessive for a woman

explanation.surface: The lady's possessions include more items besides.
explanation.definitionFit: One who etches designs into metal or glass is a kind of engraver.

clue.text: Considered to be in moderate danger

indicators.note: the answer is placed inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Something judged to be at a medium level of risk.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'modeRATE Danger'.
explanation.definitionFit: To be rated is to be assessed or judged, considered.

clue.text: Garbled denial about work being exposed

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go round the other piece
a garbled message is jumbled, so these letters are mixed up

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: A muddled denial about a job ended up revealing everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Garbled' makes LAIDEN, and 'about' wraps that round the short word for a work; 'being' is a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Laid open means uncovered or revealed to view, so exposed.

clue.text: Sign one's car has broken down

definitions.text: Sign one's car has broken down

parts.words: Sign one's car has broken down
parts.note: a notice on a vehicle being pulled behind a breakdown truck

explanation.surface: A notice that a motorist's vehicle has stopped working.
explanation.definitionFit: A car being towed displays a notice to that effect, a sign it has broken down.

clue.text: He could be one in church

indicators.note: one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: a minster is a large church
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: Someone might be found as a member of the congregation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' is a link; the whole clue also describes a clergyman, who is indeed someone in church.
explanation.definitionFit: A minister of religion, traditionally male, is the person the pronoun stands for here.

clue.text: Dandy is grasping at French craft

indicators.note: holding something means surrounding it, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: a beau is a fashionable man, a dandy

explanation.surface: A fop clutching at some French boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Bateau is the French word for a boat, a small craft.

clue.text: Bumped into brick carrier, making way

parts.note: to bump into someone is to meet them, past tense met
a hod is a builder's trough for carrying bricks

explanation.surface: Colliding with a builder's labourer while clearing a path.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A method is a way of doing something, a procedure.

clue.text: Rejected everywhere broadcasted

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard rather than read, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: throughout means in every part, everywhere

explanation.surface: Turned down after being publicised far and wide.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw out a proposal is to discard or refuse it, so rejected.
